raw_case_text: A 46-month-old male patient had a history of recurrent bronchiolitis, inability to walk, inability to speak and seizure, and he presented to our clinic with respiratory distress. A physical examination revealed retardation in neuromotor development, fever, and rales and rhonchi on lung auscultation. There was consanguinity between the patents (second cousins). The laboratory test results were as follows: WBC: 3320 /mm3, ANC: 2870/mm3, ALC: 130/mm3, Hb: 11.4 g/dL, PLT: 284000/mm3, UA: 0.6 mg/dL, IgG: 741 mg/dL, IgA: 28 mg/dL, IgM: 38 mg/dL, LP: CD3 4.2%, CD19 0.46%, CD4 2.2%, CD8 2.7%, CD3-CD16/56 90%, CD3 HLA DR 2.4%. CMV viral load (DNA quantitative) was found as 3311 IU/mL. Respiratory virus panel revealed influenza, and stool examination demonstrated the presence of rotavirus. During hospitalization in the intensive care unit, tracheal aspirate culture and skin lesion tissue fungal examination revealed Candida albicans. Bronchiolitis obliterans was found on HRCT. During the follow-up, anemia developed and a direct Coombs test was found as (+++), suggesting a diagnosis of autoimmune hemolytic anemia. In the follow-up, resistant convulsions occurred. Cranial computed tomography showed cerebral, cereballar atrophy and deepening of cerebral sulci (Fig. 1). Fully suitable HSCT from the father was planned, but the patient was lost before HSCT could be performed with a picture of resistant fever, septic shock, and multiorgan failure under multiple antibiotherapy, antifungal and antiviral treatment (Table 1). A homozygous p.R58X stop codon mutation was found in the patient, and the parents were found to have heterozygous c.172 C>T (p.Arg58Ter) mutations (Table 2).

subjective.chief_complaint: A 46-month-old boy born to consanguineous parents presented with acute respiratory distress against a background of recurrent bronchiolitis, severe neuromotor developmental delay (inability to walk or speak), and seizures.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: With a history of recurrent bronchiolitis, global psychomotor retardation, and epilepsy, the child presented with febrile respiratory distress, and during ICU hospitalization developed refractory convulsions, Coombs-positive autoimmune hemolytic anemia, polymicrobial viral and fungal infections, septic shock, and multiorgan failure.
subjective.past_medical_history: Recurrent bronchiolitis, severe neuromotor developmental delay (unable to walk or speak), and seizure disorder. Family history: born to consanguineous parents (second cousins).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for respiratory distress, fever, inability to walk or speak, and refractory convulsions.

objective.physical_examination: Fever, severe neuromotor developmental retardation, and bilateral pulmonary rales and rhonchi on chest auscultation; subsequent refractory convulsions in the ICU.
objective.routine_investigations: WBC 3,320/mm3, ANC 2,870/mm3, severe lymphopenia with ALC 130/mm3, hemoglobin 11.4 g/dL (subsequently developed anemia with 3+ positive direct Coombs test), platelets 284,000/mm3, extremely low serum uric acid 0.6 mg/dL, IgG 741 mg/dL, IgA 28 mg/dL, and IgM 38 mg/dL. Respiratory viral panel positive for influenza virus; stool examination positive for rotavirus; ICU tracheal aspirate culture and skin lesion fungal examination positive for Candida albicans.
objective.advanced_workup: Lymphocyte subset flow cytometry showed profound T- and B-cell depletion with NK-cell predominance (T-B-NK+ SCID phenotype): CD3+ 4.2%, CD4+ 2.2%, CD8+ 2.7%, CD19+ 0.46%, CD3-CD16/56+ NK cells 90%, and CD3+HLA-DR+ 2.4%. Quantitative blood CMV DNA PCR was positive at 3,311 IU/mL. Chest HRCT demonstrated bronchiolitis obliterans; cranial CT showed diffuse cerebral and cerebellar atrophy with deepened cerebral sulci. Genetic sequencing identified a homozygous nonsense mutation in the PNP (purine nucleoside phosphorylase) gene: c.172C>T (p.Arg58Ter / p.R58X), with both parents confirmed as heterozygous carriers.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis of autosomal recessive purine nucleoside phosphorylase (PNP) deficiency (confirmed by homozygous c.172C>T [p.R58X] nonsense mutation, hypouricemia of 0.6 mg/dL, severe T- and B-cell lymphopenia [ALC 130/mm3, CD3 4.2%, CD19 0.46%], neuromotor delay/cerebellar atrophy, and Coombs 3+ autoimmune hemolytic anemia) complicated by active cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection (CMV DNA viral load 3,311 IU/mL), influenza respiratory infection, rotavirus gastroenteritis, mucocutaneous/tracheal Candida albicans infection, and bronchiolitis obliterans. Despite broad-spectrum antibacterial, antifungal, and antiviral therapy in the ICU while preparing for paternal HLA-matched HSCT, the patient died of refractory fever, septic shock, and multiorgan failure prior to transplantation.
